text:
County Planning Department outlines emergency activities allowed in Special Management Area
U. N. Kim
The County of Maui Department of Planning announced on Aug. 19 that certain emergency activities are temporarily permitted within the Special Management Area (SMA) due to the state emergency proclamation related to Tropical Storm Lala.
The SMA is a designated coastal zone intended to protect natural, cultural, and recreational resources. Property owners and residents can verify if their property falls within this area by using the County’s Land Use Viewer webpage and selecting “Special Management Area (SMA).”
County Planning Director Jacky Takakura said, “The Department recognizes that property owners and public agencies may need to act quickly to address storm damage and protect public health and safety. The Governor’s proclamation provides flexibility for necessary emergency work while we continue to encourage everyone working along the coast to minimize impacts to neighboring properties and Maui County’s natural and cultural resources.”
Governor Josh Green issued a statewide emergency proclamation on Aug. 13 in anticipation of Tropical Storm Lala's potential impacts from damaging winds, heavy rain, and surf. The proclamation suspends HRS Chapter 205A as needed for government agencies preparing for, responding to, or recovering from the emergency. However, this suspension is specifically intended for necessary response and recovery activities related to Tropical Storm Lala; it does not constitute a general waiver of SMA requirements for unrelated development.
Permitted activities under the proclamation include removal of storm debris without unnecessarily expanding disturbance areas; temporary stabilization or protection of damaged structures; emergency repairs such as fixing roofs or windows; repair or replacement of damaged public infrastructure including roads, bridges, drainage facilities, water systems, and electrical infrastructure; as well as other actions needed to address hazards caused by the storm.
The suspension does not automatically waive other required permits under county, state, or federal laws—permits such as building or electrical may still be required depending on proposed work. The disaster relief period currently continues through Aug. 27 unless terminated earlier or superseded by another proclamation. Once lifted, standard HRS Chapter 205A requirements will resume.
